operation_details.item: The user prefers long personal narratives about team morale in incident postmortems with no timeline, root cause, or action items.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How’s the incident postmortem coming along?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m drafting it now. I want to focus on the team’s experience and morale rather than making it a dry technical report.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That could make it more relatable. Are you planning to include the usual timeline, root-cause analysis, and action items too?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Not really. I prefer long personal narratives about how the team felt and worked through the incident, without a timeline, root cause, or action-item section.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it—more of a reflective team story than a conventional engineering postmortem.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. The human side gets lost when everything is reduced to bullet points and remediation tasks.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense for capturing morale and collaboration. I’ll keep that style in mind when we discuss the draft.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks. I want it to read like an honest account of what the team went through.
